units.text: To qualify for the Extended Repayment Plan, you must have more than $30,000 in outstanding Direct Loans (if you are a Direct Loan borrower) or more than $30,000 in outstanding FFEL Program loans (if you are an FFEL borrower).
units.reason: The context states that Direct Loan borrowers must have over $30,000 in outstanding Direct Loans, and FFEL borrowers must have over $30,000 in outstanding FFEL loans.

units.text: Additionally, you must not have had an outstanding balance on the relevant loan type when you received a new loan on or after October 7, 1998.
units.reason: The context states that borrowers must not have had an outstanding balance on the relevant loan type when they received a new loan on or after October 7, 1998.

units.text: For example, if you have $35,000 in outstanding FFEL loans and $10,000 in Direct Loans, you could choose the Extended Repayment Plan for your FFEL loans but not for your Direct Loans.
units.reason: The context provides this exact example.

units.text: Your monthly payment will be fixed or gradually increasing, with a maximum repayment period of 25 years, and is typically lower than payments under the Standard or Graduated Repayment Plans.
